# shareit

> shareit ({{SITE_URL}}) is a personal sharing server. With its share key, an agent can publish HTML
> plans (living documents updated in place) and run polls (single- or multi-choice, live results).

All API requests go to `{{SITE_URL}}/api/...` and need the share key in the `X-Share-Key` header. The
owner gives you the key; it is shown on `{{SITE_URL}}/admin/plans`. Never put the key in a plan, a
poll, or any URL. Errors are JSON `{ "error": "..." }`: `400` bad input, `401` bad key, `404` not
found, `409` slug taken, `413` too large.

## Plans

A plan is one self-contained HTML document, served at `{{SITE_URL}}/p/<slug>.html`. Its `<title>`
becomes the plan's name. It is sandboxed: inline CSS/JS and `https:` assets work, forms do not post.

Create — the body is the raw HTML, response is `201`:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST \
  -H "X-Share-Key: $SHAREIT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8" \
  --data-binary @plan.html \
  {{SITE_URL}}/api/plans
# {"slug":"Ab3def4Gh5jk","url":"{{SITE_URL}}/p/Ab3def4Gh5jk.html","updateUrl":"{{SITE_URL}}/api/plans/Ab3def4Gh5jk.html"}
```

Update — `PUT` the full replacement HTML to `updateUrl`; the public URL stays the same. Keep the
`updateUrl` from the create response if you will revise the plan later.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X PUT \
  -H "X-Share-Key: $SHAREIT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8" \
  --data-binary @plan.html \
  {{SITE_URL}}/api/plans/Ab3def4Gh5jk.html
```

## Polls

A poll is served at `{{SITE_URL}}/poll/<slug>`; share that URL (it unfurls with a preview card in
Slack). Voters give their name once and can change their vote until the poll closes. JSON in, JSON
out.

Fields:

- `title` (string, required) — the question.
- `options` (array, required, 2–50) — each is Markdown or HTML, e.g. `"[Go-karting](https://…) — $45"`.
  On create, plain strings. On update, see "Changing options" below.
- `description` (string or null) — Markdown or HTML shown above the options: budget, dates, context.
- `slug` (string) — custom URL part, letters/numbers/`-`/`_`, max 40. Random if omitted.
- `multi` (boolean, default `false`) — `true` lets voters pick any number of options.
- `closesAt` (ISO 8601 with offset, or null) — when voting stops. `null` means open until closed.

Create — response is `201` with the full poll:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST \
  -H "X-Share-Key: $SHAREIT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "What should we do for the November team event?",
    "description": "Budget is **$60/person**. Pick everything you would enjoy.",
    "slug": "november-event",
    "multi": true,
    "closesAt": "2026-11-01T17:00:00-04:00",
    "options": [
      "[Go-karting](https://example.com/karts) at the speedway",
      "Escape room — two rooms of 6",
      "Cooking class"
    ]
  }' \
  {{SITE_URL}}/api/polls
```

Poll response shape (create, read, and update all return this):

```json
{
  "id": "…",
  "slug": "november-event",
  "title": "What should we do for the November team event?",
  "description": "Budget is **$60/person**. Pick everything you would enjoy.",
  "multi": true,
  "closesAt": "2026-11-01T21:00:00.000Z",
  "closed": false,
  "url": "{{SITE_URL}}/poll/november-event",
  "apiUrl": "{{SITE_URL}}/api/polls/november-event",
  "voterCount": 2,
  "options": [{ "id": "opt1…", "content": "[Go-karting](…) at the speedway", "votes": 2 }],
  "voters": [{ "name": "Sam", "optionIds": ["opt1…"], "votedAt": "2026-10-21T14:03:00.000Z" }]
}
```

Read results: `GET {{SITE_URL}}/api/polls/<slug>`. List all polls: `GET {{SITE_URL}}/api/polls`
(slug, title, closed, url, apiUrl, createdAt for each).

Update: `PATCH {{SITE_URL}}/api/polls/<slug>` with only the fields to change.

- Close now: `{ "closesAt": "<current time, ISO 8601>" }`. Reopen: `{ "closesAt": null }`.
- Changing options: `options` replaces the whole list, in order. To keep an option and its votes,
  pass `{ "id": "<option id from GET>", "content": "…" }`; plain strings are new options. Any
  existing option you leave out is deleted with its votes — GET the poll first and send back the
  ids you want to keep.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X PATCH \
  -H "X-Share-Key: $SHAREIT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "options": [{ "id": "opt1…", "content": "Go-karting (Nov 14)" }, "Bowling"] }' \
  {{SITE_URL}}/api/polls/november-event
```

## Tips

- One question per poll. For a team event, poll the activity first, then a second poll for the date.
- Keep option text short; put details in links or the description. The first ~60 characters of each
  option show on the Slack preview card.
- Tell the owner the poll `url` to share, not the `apiUrl`.
